title: Snowflake's SQL text: escapes, comments, intervals
verdict: backslash escapes in literals; `//` comments; interval strings need commas
description: A backslash escapes in a quoted literal (`'a\\b'` has 3 characters, `'\n'` is a newline, `'\u00e9'` `é`); `$$…$$` is raw. `//` starts a comment, like `--`. Unquoted identifiers fold to upper case.

`INTERVAL '1 day 2 hours'` is a syntax error, `INTERVAL '1 day, 2 hours'` works. `INTERVAL '1.5 seconds'` adds 2 seconds, rounded, where `'1500 milliseconds'` adds 1.5. `TIMESTAMP - TIMESTAMP` is an `INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND`, which the Python connector does not serialise to JSON.
reference: Not in the model. sverify's SQL doubles backslashes and writes control characters as escapes (`str_lit`), quotes every identifier, writes no `//` and no intervals (`DATEADD` instead).

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)
provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
